extracted.intended_audience: Catholic students, catechists, catechumens preparing for religious instruction or examination
extracted.subtask_description: A lesson-by-lesson question bank (catechism) enumerating specific doctrinal and practice questions learners are expected to know and answer for Catholic religious instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 10 — effects, supernatural, merit, virtue, neighbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 357–369: (examples) 357. What do we mean by an effect? 358. What does 'supernatural' mean? 359. What is merit? 360. What is a virtue? 361. What is a vice? 362–363. Does habit excuse us for the sins committed through it? When will habit excuse us for the sin? 364. Why do we believe revealed truths? 365–368. Who is our neighbor? What example did Our Lord give to explain this? How do we love our neighbor as ourselves? Why should we love our neighbor? 369. Can we merit the grace of perseverance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A checklist of discrete doctrinal definitions and moral-application questions learners must be able to answer; intended for memorization and oral or written examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 11 — early religion, prophets, Church works, persecutions, pastors
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 370–385: (examples) 370. When did men begin to speak different languages? 371. Who were the prophets? 372. Give a short history of religion before the time of Christ. 373. What are the chief works of the Church? 374–377. Why are our churches holy? What are the catacombs, and why were they made? What are altar stones? Why are relics placed in them? 378–380. How many general persecutions of the Church were there? Tell what you know of these persecutions. What lessons do we learn from the sufferings of the early Christians? 381–385. Who are 'lawful pastors'? Could anyone be Pope without being Bishop of Rome? What does 'vicar' mean? Why are Catholics called Roman? How could a Protestant be saved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on historical knowledge, terminology, and pastoral/missional implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 12 — attributes and authority of the Church, Papal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 386–419: (examples) 386. What is an attribute? 387. What is authority? 388. Why is it sinful to resist lawful authority? 389–391. What does 'cathedra' mean? Why is the bishop's church called cathedral? How do we know when the Pope speaks 'ex cathedra'? 392–396. What is required that the Pope may so speak? Is the Pope infallible in everything he says? What do you mean by 'faith and morals'? How many Popes from St. Peter to Pius XI? Why should we have the greatest respect for the opinions of the Holy Father on any subject? 397–404. Why must the Pope sometimes speak on political matters? Can the Pope commit sin? What do we mean by the 'temporal power' of the Pope?... 405–419. How is the Church one in government and doctrine? What is the hierarchy? Could a person be a Catholic and not believe all the Church teaches? Why does the Church use Latin? Does the Church by defining truths make new doctrines? (includes questions about Luther and Protestants.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes doctrinal authority, papal prerogatives, infallibility limits and historical-political relations of the Church.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 13 — sacraments: signs, uses, disposition, ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 420–437: (examples) 420. What three things are necessary to make a Sacrament? 421–425. What is the outward sign in Baptism? Why is water used? What is the outward sign in Confirmation? Why is oil used? What is the use of the outward sign in the Sacraments? 426–437. In what ways does the life of the soul resemble the life of the body? What does a 'Sacrament of the dead' mean? In what ways can we commit sacrilege? What is the sacramental grace given in Penance? What are the 'right dispositions' for Penance, for Holy Eucharist? Conditional Baptism and its use; Matrimony sign; who can give sacraments; can sacraments be given to the dead?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers theology of sacraments, ritual signs, ministerial roles, dispositions, and sacramental exceptions (conditional, to the dead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 14 — Scripture, sacramental effects, baptismal questions, martyrs, patron saints
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 438–461: (examples) 438. What is an heir? 439–441. Why is the Bible called the Old and New Testament? What does each contain? 442–446. Difference between Baptism and Penance in remission of guilt and punishment; could one gain an indulgence immediately after Baptism? What does 'temporal punishment' mean? Where will persons go who have never sinned and who die without Baptism? 446–461. Ordinary minister of a Sacrament; baptizing infants against parental will; private vs solemn Baptism ceremonies and meanings; baptistery; 'pomps' of the devil; martyrdom; catechumens; patron saints; sponsors and godparents; names to be given in Baptism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine of Scripture and Sacraments, practical and ceremonial questions related to Baptism, martyrdom, saints and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 15 — sacramental symbolism and profession of religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 462–464: (examples) 462. What does balm in the chrism signify? 463. Why should we be proud of the Catholic religion? 464. When are we required to profess our religion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short set of questions on sacramental symbolism and the duty/profession of faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 16 — Beatitudes and Christian poverty of spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 465–471: (examples) 465. Why is the devil wiser than we are? 466. Who made the Beatitudes? 467. Where did Our Lord generally preach? 468–471. What do the Beatitudes teach? How is a person 'poor in spirit'? How can the rich be 'poor in spirit'? Explain the other Beatitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral and spiritual interpretation of the Beatitudes and the Christian life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 17 — Penance, absolution, confession preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 472–480: (examples) 472. How does the institution of Penance show the goodness of Our Lord? 473. What is absolution? 474–480. How do you know Our Lord could forgive sins? How does the power to forgive imply obligation of confession? How do we prepare for confession? Best method of examining conscience? Most important part of the Sacrament? What kind of sorrow should we have for our sins? When should you say the penance given in confession?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on sacramental theology of Penance, practical confession preparation, and interior dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 18 — contrition, attrition, occasions of sin
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 481–484: (examples) 481. When is our contrition perfect? 482. What is attrition? 483–484. How many kinds of occasions of sin are there? Why must we avoid occasions of sin?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short doctrinal and practical distinctions regarding sorrow for sin and avoidance of temptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 19 — confession logistics, penance history, Lent, works of mercy
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 485–510: (examples) 485. Who is a 'duly authorized' priest? 486–489. How can a dumb man make his confession? What can one do who cannot remember sins? How confess in danger of death when priest does not understand language? 489–496. Is it wrong to accuse ourselves of sins we have not committed? Why foolish to conceal sins? How were ancient churches divided? How did early Christians do penance? Explain temporal and eternal punishment for sin. Is confession worthless if you forget to say penance? 495–510. What is Lent? What is almsgiving? Distinguish spiritual and corporal works of mercy; when obliged to admonish the sinner; Crusades; pilgrim; relief from works of mercy; religious; hermit; general confession; who are scrupulous persons?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines canonical/practical questions on confession with historical and pastoral topics (penance practices, works of mercy, religious life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 20 — confessor's duties and confessional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 511–516: (examples) 511. When is it well to add to our confession a sin of our past life? 512–514. What duties does the priest perform in the confessional? Show how he is judge, father, teacher, and physician. Why is it well to confess always to the same priest? 515–516. Can you have half your sins forgiven? When will perfect contrition blot out mortal sin?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes pastoral role of confessor, continuity of confession, and effects of contrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 21 — rewards, indulgences, intentions, historical penance
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 517–524: (examples) 517. How does God reward us for good works done in a state of mortal sin? 518. Is it easy to gain a plenary indulgence? Why? 519–523. What works are generally enjoined for indulgences? What does praying for a 'person's intention' mean? How can we have the intention of gaining an indulgence? What does 'an indulgence of 40 days' mean? 523–524. Why did early Christians do more severe penance than we do? Are indulgences attached to anything but prayers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal understanding of indulgences, intention, and historical comparison of penance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 22 — Eucharist, Mass parts, vessels, vestments, adoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 525–561: (examples) 525. What does 'Eucharist' mean? 526. What is the difference between Holy Eucharist and Holy Communion? 527–536. What did Our Lord do at Cana? Is Our Lord's body in the Eucharist living or dead? How do you know you receive body and blood under appearance of bread alone? Why does the Church not give the Eucharist under the appearance of wine to the people? Could it do so? How long does Our Lord remain in Holy Communion? What is the ciborium? At what part of the Mass are the words of consecration said? What are the parts of the Mass? 537–561. Sacristy, priest preparations, chalice, paten, purificator, pall, host, source of the host, vestments and their colors, Offertory, Canon, Elevation, tabernacle, Benediction, monstrance, cope, humeral veil, reasons for vestments, fasting rules, evening Mass and Communion timing, genuflection and ritual actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive checklist of Eucharistic theology, liturgical elements, vessels, vesture, and devotional practices used for instruction and liturgical literacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 23 — fasting, Viaticum, first Mass
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 562–564: (examples) 562. What should we do if we break our fast before Holy Communion? 563. When is Holy Communion called the 'Viaticum'? 564. Who offered the first Sacrifice of the Holy Mass?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rules on fasting and Eucharist in relation to last rites and sacrificial theology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 24 — Eucharist as sacrifice, types of sacrifice, simony, spiritual Communion
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 565–578: (examples) 565. When is the Holy Eucharist a sacrifice? 566. When a Sacrament? 567–570. What was the temple of the Pantheon in Rome? Who are pagans, idolaters, heathens? How many kinds of sacrifice had the Israelites? 570–576. How is the Mass a sacrifice? What is the league of the Sacred Heart? Why was it established? Origin of offering priests money for Mass intention? What is the sin of simony? 576–578. How are the fruits of the Mass divided? What is a spiritual Communion? How is it made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines sacrificial theology, pastoral history, liturgical fruits, and abuses (simony) with devotional practice (spiritual communion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 25 — Extreme Unction, sick rites, ministers, tonsure, kinds of Masses
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 579–611: (examples) 579. What does 'unction' mean? 580–582. How often in their lives are Catholics anointed? Is it called Extreme Unction even when the person recovers after receiving it? What parts of the body are anointed? 583–589. When should the priest be sent for in sickness? What should you do if the sick Catholic refuses the priest? How is sickness a benefit to some? What Sacraments are never given in the Church? What should you prepare when priest comes for Viaticum or Extreme Unction? How is the Blessed Sacrament carried to the sick? Who are 'other ministers of the Church' besides bishops and priests? 590–596. What is the tonsure? Of what does it remind the priest? Duties and privileges of other ministers; how many kinds of Masses; do they differ in value; who is the 'celebrant'? What does the 'master of ceremonies' do? 597–611. Requiem Mass, Vespers, obligations, cardinals, monsignor, vicar general, diocese, parish, rector vs pastor, suffragan bishops, the pallium and who can wear it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive practical, canonical, and ceremonial Qs about pastoral care of the sick, liturgical roles, clerical offices and rites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 26 — marriage: lawfulness, impediments, civil effects, mixed marriages
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 612–637: (examples) 612. When are persons lawfully married? 613–616. When was marriage first instituted? What sin to marry unlawfully? What are 'impediments to marriage'? What things should persons tell the priest when making arrangements for marriage? 617–626. Can persons marry invalidly without knowing it? What evils follow divorce? Why should children study? What is meant by 'civil effects of marriage'? What are chief evils of 'mixed marriage'? What is a 'mixed marriage'? 623–637. When are motives for marriage 'worthy'? How should persons choose for marriage? Parental injustices in marriage choices; holy oil, its blessing and uses; how many kinds of holy oil and in which sacraments oil is used; can persons receive Matrimony more than once? Where and at what time should Catholics be married? Was there a Sacrament of Matrimony before Our Lord? Were Old Law marriages valid and how did they differ?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinal and pastoral instruction concerning sacramental marriage, canonical impediments, civil implications and pastoral preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 27 — sacramentals, devotions, rosary, Marian topics, religious orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 638–676: (examples) 638. Can the Church change the number of sacramentals? Why? 639–645. Why is it necessary to bless yourself properly? When are candles blessed? Of what do candles on the altar remind us? When are ashes blessed? Of what do they remind us? Of what do the palms remind us? What is the difference between a cross and a crucifix? 646–666. What is the Rosary? How do we say the beads? What are 'Mysteries of the Rosary' and how many? Name them. What is the Magnificat? Who baptized Our Lord? Was John's baptism a Sacrament? To whom did Our Lord give example by His hidden life? What did the Church do for slaves? What do 'I.N.R.I.' mean? Did Our Lord claim to be king of the Jews? Why was He put to death? Who was St. John the Evangelist? What is the Apocalypse? How long did the Blessed Virgin live on earth after Ascension? What is the 'Assumption' of the Blessed Virgin? What proof have we? On what days are the Mysteries said? What does 'I.H.S.' mean? What is the scapular and why wear it? Brown scapular and kinds, seven dolors and beads; religious orders, vows, founding reasons and varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive coverage of sacramentals, popular devotions (Rosary, scapular), Marian doctrines and history of religious life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 28 — prayer types and meditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 677–683: (examples) 677. How many kinds of prayer are there? 678. What is 'meditation'? 679. What should we do before praying? 680–683. What do you know of St. Monica? Of St. Augustine? Why does God not always grant our prayers? If prayer is necessary for salvation, how can infants be saved who die without having prayed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction on prayer forms, preparation for prayer, examples from saints, and theological questions about efficacy and infants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 29 — law before Moses, types of Israelite laws, Commandments
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 684–690: (examples) 684. Were people obliged to keep the Commandments before Moses? 685–687. How many kinds of laws had the Israelites? When were these laws abolished? How were the Commandments given to Moses? 688–690. What was manna? What is the difference between the Commandments of God and the commandments of the Church? What does 'love thy neighbor as thyself' mean?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on moral and positive law distinctions and historical origin of Mosaic law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 30 — idolatry, superstitions, mediums, heresies, spread of Christianity
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 691–707: (examples) 691. How did the Israelites come to worship false gods? 692–700. How do we sometimes worship strange gods? What are 'fortune tellers'? Why is going to fortune tellers a sin? What are spells and charms? Are medals or scapulars charms? What are dreams? Did God ever use them to make His will known? Why not now? What are mediums and spiritists? 701–707. How do bad Catholics injure the Church? Why did Christianity spread rapidly? Who are atheists, deists, infidels, heretics, apostates, schismatics? Are all religions equally true? Why is presumption a great sin? How are we frequently presumptuous? Are heretics Christians?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses superstitions, occult practices, religious errors, and apologetics concerning the uniqueness and spread of Christianity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 31 — help to salvation, saints, relics, suitability of Catholicism
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 708–716: (examples) 708. What help does God give us to save our souls? 709–715. How do we honor God by praying to the saints? What is a relic? Have we any relics of Our Lord's body? Why? Why does the Catholic religion suit all classes of persons? Why are there so many kinds of Protestants? Does the Bible contain all the truths of our religion? How did God honor the relics of saints? Give an example. 716. When did the Jewish religion cease to be the true religion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine on intercession of saints, relics, ecclesial universality, and relation of Scripture to Church teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 32 — oaths, blasphemy, secret societies, holy days, proper reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 717–731: (examples) 717. Is it a sin to use the words of Scripture in a bad sense? 718. What is a perjurer? 719–725. Why was John the Baptist put to death? Why is it sinful to be a member of a secret society? When is an oath rash? Difference between blasphemy and cursing; can we blaspheme by action? Tell what happened to Julian the Apostate. Are there any holy days not of obligation? 726–731. How is the Sunday well kept? What is a real Catholic newspaper? What books should be found in every Catholic family? What is meant by the Old Law? What by the New? Are we bound to keep an unlawful oath?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral theology as applied to speech, public order, secret societies, media, and liturgical obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 33 — magistrates, suffering, virtues, suicide, prudence about reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 732–742: (examples) 732. What do we mean by 'magistrates'? 733. What should we remember when unjustly punished? 734–736. How does suffering make us more like Our Lord and His Blessed Mother? Why did the Blessed Virgin suffer many trials? 736–741. What is contempt? What is stubbornness? Why is suicide a mortal sin? What is revenge? Why guard most carefully the Sixth Commandment? 741–742. Why guard against bad reading? Why seek advice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers social order, virtues in suffering, grave sins (suicide, revenge), and prudential guidance on reading and counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 34 — Seventh Commandment, restitution, detraction, calumny, truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 743–764: (examples) 743. In how many ways may we violate the Seventh Commandment? 744–750. Why unkind and ungrateful not to pay debts? Is receiver of stolen goods as bad as the thief? In how many ways may we share in the sin of another? If you bought a stolen article unknowingly, are you obliged to give it up? What must you do with found articles? What if you lost or destroyed what you stole? 750–756. Can we always make restitution by giving to the poor? Is it a sin to delay restitution? What must a person do who cannot restore? What will excuse us for telling another's faults? How can you know when you have injured another's character? What is detraction? What is calumny? What is slander? 758–764. How can you make reparation for injuring another's character? Are you bound to do so? What is 'rash judgment'? What is backbiting? Is it sinful to listen to backbiting or slander? Why wrong to tell another's secrets or read another's letters? What does 'covet' mean?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed moral-ethical questions on justice, restitution, truth-telling, and offenses against reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 35 — Mass attendance, excuses, divine office, fasting/abstinence obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 765–773: (examples) 765. What is meant by a 'serious reason' for missing Mass? 766–768. What excuses do some give for not hearing Mass? Why is it wrong to come late? On what day do we keep a saint's feast? 769–773. What is the 'divine office'? How is it divided? Who are excused from fasting? Who must abstain from flesh-meat on fast days and days of abstinence? Is every fast-day a day of abstinence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liturgical obligations and legitimate exemptions; pastoral explanation of 'serious reason' and liturgical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 36 — confession frequency, biblical history, dispensations, excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 774–790: (examples) 774. Why should we go to confession even when we have not committed sin since our last confession? 775–779. When is Trinity Sunday? How was the Holy Land divided? Who were the 'Levites'? What were 'first fruits' and tithes? Why was Cain's sacrifice displeasing to God? 780–786. What relations are within the third degree of kindred? What is a 'dispensation' granted by the Church? What is meant by the 'natural law'? When can we obey state laws regarding marriage? What is 'excommunication' and what effect has it? 786–790. Who are excluded from Christian burial? How does the Church show displeasure when Catholics marry persons not Catholics? How should persons prepare for marriage? Are women ever allowed with heads uncovered? Can priest say a 'nuptial Mass' for a husband or wife after their death?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixes pastoral practice on confession with canonical matters (dispensations, excommunication), biblical/historical items, and marriage preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson 37 — judgment, Purgatory, Hell, Heaven, beatific vision, eschatology
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions 791–810: (examples) 791. Where will the particular judgment be held? 792–797. How will it take place? Will sentence at particular judgment be changed at general judgment? How can we prepare daily for judgment? Who will be judged at the general judgment? How will it take place? 797–804. What do we mean by the 'pain of loss'? By the 'pain of sense' that the damned suffer? Why can we not imagine the sufferings of Hell? How does the fire of Hell differ from our fire? Will there be a Purgatory after the general judgment? Why must there be a Purgatory now? 803–810. If God loves those in Purgatory, why does He punish them? Why show respect to bodies of the dead? What does 'faithful departed' mean? What does 'rest in peace' mean? What does 'seeing God face to face' mean if God has no face? What is the beatific vision? Of what does our happiness in Heaven consist? How long will Purgatory last?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive eschatological checklist covering judgment, Hell, Purgatory, Heaven and related devotional practices and beliefs; intended as an index of required doctrinal knowledge.
